newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia arrests Britons with $50 mln of cocaine.
newsitem.headline: Colombia arrests Britons with $50 mln of cocaine.

text.p: Three Britons have been arrested in Colombia's Caribbean port of Barranquilla as they allegedly tried to smuggle cocaine worth an estimated $50 million out of the country, officials said on Saturday.
Michael Hayne, his son Alan and a third man David Maurice Shaw were seized by agents of the DAS security service Friday evening on the quay in Barranquilla.
A DAS spokesman alleged 427 pounds (194 kg) of high purity cocaine was found aboard their U.S. registered boat named Perla del Mar.
"We estimate this cocaine would have been worth about $50 million. We don't know where it was destined for," a spokesman for the DAS in Barranquilla said.

The three men are currently in custody in the city's El Bosque jail. The spokesman said he did not know the men's home city in Britain. He added that Shaw had entered Colombia on many occasions in the past and that the Haynes had entered Colombia from Venezuela but did not have valid entry stamps.
British embassy officials were unavailable for comment on the arrests.
